body:
## Quick answer

For Chinese New Year (**Saturday, 6 February 2027**), wear **red, pink, magenta or wine with gold** – colours of luck and celebration – and keep it comfortable and modest, because open houses mean a long day of visiting elders and eating. Avoid an all-black or all-white outfit. Order a ready size by **9 January** (custom fit by **2 January**) for delivery to Singapore or Malaysia before the holiday.

## What to wear to a Chinese New Year open house

| Occasion | Pick | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Reunion dinner with friends' families | Anarkali in magenta or wine with gold work | Festive and elegant, easy to sit in |
| Daytime house visits | Kurta set or short kurti in rani pink | Light and breathable in the heat |
| Office lo hei lunch | Embroidered kurti with trousers | Smart, colourful, not too dressy |

Gold zardozi, gota or lace adds the touch of gold that the season loves – no heavy jewellery needed.

## Colours to choose and avoid

- **Choose:** red, magenta, rani pink, wine, coral, orange and gold
- **Go easy on:** an all-black or all-white outfit, which many families keep for mourning
- **Tip:** in Singapore and Malaysia's heat, georgette and cotton are cooler than velvet for daytime visits; keep velvet for an air-conditioned dinner

## Delivery to Singapore and Malaysia

- Order a ready size by **9 January 2027** and a custom-fit piece by **2 January** for delivery before 6 February
- Prices are shown and charged in US$ – your bank converts the amount
- The [festival calendar](/festival/) lists every last order date, including Thaipusam and Deepavali

- Ready sizes are dispatched in 7–10 working days, custom fit in 10–15, then 5–10 business days for delivery

faq.a: Saturday, 6 February 2027. Singapore and Malaysia have public holidays on 6 and 7 February.

faq.q: What colour should I wear to a Chinese New Year open house?
faq.a: Red, pink, magenta, wine, coral or orange, ideally with a touch of gold. These are seen as lucky, festive colours. Avoid an all-black or all-white outfit.

faq.q: Is it okay to wear an Indian outfit to Chinese New Year?
faq.a: Yes – a festive Indian outfit in a lucky colour is a warm, respectful choice for a friend's open house, especially in Singapore and Malaysia where many families celebrate together.
